description: A developer skill verification oracle. Validators independently query GitHub's search index and agree on one level: EXPERT, PROFICIENT, BEGINNER or NONE. A username is bound to one wallet by register_identity, so a consumer pays the developer rather than whoever quotes their name.

studiodev.verified: 23/23 at deploy time (node test/deploy_studiodev.mjs) and 21/21 read-only since (node test/check_deployment.mjs --network=studiodev), including that the consumer reads THIS oracle ACROSS the contract boundary.
studiodev.carries_the_identity_fix: Yes, and it is EXERCISED ON CHAIN rather than asserted. node test/prove_identity_gate.mjs: 14/14. alice registered `torvalds`; bob was refused the registration, refused the claim, allowed to buy his own verification of the same username - which made him its verified_by - and refused the claim AGAIN; alice then claimed and was paid 1 GEN. That last pair is the whole point: binding to verified_by would have paid the thief.
studiodev.carries_the_consensus_fix: Yes, and this deployment finally exercises it against a real validator quorum. Verification 1 is torvalds/C, RESOLVED EXPERT with repo_count 8 and content_hash 4d9b2c5e983bec94 - the same 8 repositories the offline fixture and the round-1 probe measured. _compare_key and the _apply coherence gate are in the deployed bytes.
studiodev.fees: studio-dev runs the fee policy ENABLED and exposes no feeManagerContract, so the SDK cannot derive a deposit: genlayer-js 1.1.8 has no `fees` argument at all and every deploy reverts at the consensus contract with no reason given. 2.0.0-rc.1 is installed alongside as `genlayer-js-rc` for this network only. estimateFeesDistribution() is NOT enough - it carries feeValue 0 and the contract answers FeeValueMustBeNonZero(1); estimateTransactionFees() adds the ~0.1 GEN deposit. AND A WRITE THAT EMITS A TRANSFER NEEDS MORE: a bounty payout is a message, messages are funded from a per-message allocation, and without one the transaction is ACCEPTED while the execution errors `fee no_matching_allocation # external` - the bounty simply stays OPEN with no revert reason anywhere. estimateTransactionFeesForWrite() simulates the call and derives the allocation. Fund with sim_fundAccount, whose amount must be a HEX STRING - a JS Number serialises as 1e+21 and the node answers 'amount must be a positive integer'.

superseded.why: Pre-identity-binding. claim_bounty on that consumer paid whichever wallet quoted a verified username, so any passer-by could collect another developer's bounty. Superseded rather than deleted: the addresses are in the previous submission.

superseded_consumer.why: DO NOT USE. Deployed before gl.get_contract_at was migrated to gl.contract.get_at. It did not fail loudly: SkillConsumer wraps every oracle read in `except Exception` so an unreachable oracle refunds instead of reverting, so the contract deployed clean, reported the right oracle address from get_terms, and silently degraded EVERY lookup to 'oracle unreachable'.
